tracks.narration: A current source pushes I in into two parallel resistors — how does the current split between them?
Both resistors sit across the same two nodes, so they share the same voltage V across them.
Ohm's law gives the branch currents I one and I two, and they add up to I in — solve it and the smaller resistor takes the bigger share.
Scrub R two. Make it small and the current pours through R two; make it large and the current crowds back into R one.
Current divides inversely to resistance — the easy path wins.
